title: Automatic Construction of Strong Simple Baselines
abstract: arXiv:2610.40700v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: To rigorously establish the value of a novel deep learning method, it must be compared against appropriate baselines. As deep learning has become increasingly common in the physical and life sciences, there have been numerous cases in which apparent progress has turned out to be an artifact of omitted or missing baselines. In this work, we investigate whether this problem can be mitigated by using large language models to automate the construction of baselines. We assemble 36 supervised classification and regression tasks from peer-reviewed studies in Nature, Science, and Cell-family journals that investigate novel deep learning methods for scientific applications. We then use a language model to construct simple baselines for each task. These automatically constructed baselines are strong, recovering a median of 95.5% (mean 85.7%) of the gap between a trivial predictor and the score of the deep learning model. tldr: 该研究利用大型语言模型为36个科学研究任务自动构建简单基线，发现这些基线表现强劲，可恢复平凡预测器与深度学习模型得分之间差距的95.5%，从而有效检验深度学习方法声称的进展。
en_tdlr: This study uses large language models to automatically construct simple baselines for 36 scientific tasks, showing these baselines are strong—recovering a median of 95.5% of the gap between a trivial predictor and the deep learning model's score—thereby validating claimed progress of deep learning methods.
